sprite_reading: Verified on tools/dinkex/out/sprites/351-359: dull blonde hair worn up and full, red dress with short puffed sleeves, bare forearms, black belt, floor-length gathered skirt with vertical fold stripes, stout build.

third_party.use: dress weave (colour detail, normal, roughness), recoloured red, with authored stains
belt and soles: grain normal/roughness, recoloured

third_party.asset_id: base mesh head/hands (shipped fit) + CC0_BaseMesh.obj arm faces, middleage_caucasian_female skin albedo, eyebrow001, eyelashes01
third_party.use: head and hand topology with shipped weights; forearms re-fitted from the base mesh and welded to the hands; albedo is the base of the authored skin set; brow and lash cards

authored_here: dress (bodice, lofted puffed sleeves, collar band, pleated skirt with authored skinning), belt and buckle, shoes; bun groom (combed cap, coiled bun, hairline cards) and strand atlas; eyeballs and eye texture; skin colour zones, age lines, pore/crease normal, roughness, SSS map; all bakes
importer_changes: New asset name SK_Mother_Photoreal (4 LOD FBX in Mother/Export). Same 89-bone SK_Mannequin skeleton, bone names, hierarchy and rest pose as the shipped SK_Mother; existing clips apply unchanged. No actions are embedded (the shipped candidate has none either).

Material slots change from [MI_Mother_Skin, MI_Mother_Eyes, MI_Mother_Hair, MI_Mother_BrowLash, MI_Mother_Wardrobe] to [MI_Mother_PR_Skin, MI_Mother_PR_Eyes, MI_Mother_PR_Hair, MI_Mother_PR_Outfit, MI_Mother_PR_Gear]: still five slots, same convention as SK_Dink_Photoreal (brows/lashes are cards inside the Hair slot; wardrobe split into Outfit 4K and Gear 2K).

Each slot has its own BC/N/ORM set; Hair is masked/two-sided with alpha in BC; Gear uses ORM.B metallic; Skin has an extra SSS map (rgb scatter colour x thickness). Normal maps are OpenGL (+Y): keep normal_flip_green true.
Textures: Skin 4096, Outfit 4096, Gear 2048, Hair 2048, Eyes 1024.

Skin weights: head and hands keep the shipped weights; the new bare-arm skin and all garments take weights by surface transfer from the Manny reference (used transiently, not delivered), as the shipped candidates did; skirts carry authored pelvis/thigh/calf weights; plates and buckles are rigid on one or two bones.
A Physics Asset still has to be generated in Unreal. UV uniqueness is per slot (see uv_per_slot); the validator's whole-mesh UV_OVERLAP error is expected with five texture sets.
review_renders: Review/r4_skirt.png (walk pose pair from two sides, turn front/back)
budget_note: LOD0 about 29.7k triangles: over the 20k soft target, under the 35k hard cap. Head keeps the MakeHuman topology (about 8.6k), hands were thinned to half, hair is about 3k, the dress about 9k.
skirt_check: Tools/check_poke.py, boots against the dress below the knee, shipped walk samples + a turn: 0 boot vertices outside the skirt in idle, 1-23 of about 300 in the walk samples (the trailing heel lifts the back hem and shows below it); before the calf-weighted back hem it was 31-73.
known_weaknesses: Not photoreal at 1 m; passes as a woman in a red dress at gameplay distance. Last review round (r4) still faulted everything below.

Face: built on the shipped middle-aged MakeHuman head with authored age lines, bags and jowls, but it still reads younger than 40-45 and somewhat boyish (round smooth cheeks, large eyes); no expression shapes, no teeth.

Hair: the pulled-back hair is one combed alpha-edged shell plus a coiled bun and a few hairline cards. At 1 m it reads as a moulded cap: regular grooves, a saw-tooth hairline, a dark gap where the bun meets the cap. The layered-card version (r1, r2) read as thatch and was dropped.

Neck: the shipped neck skin stops at z 1.53 m, so the dress has a high standing band instead of an open neckline; a dark slit shows beside the band on the character's right in the close-up and a pale sliver on the left.

Bodice is tight and smooth compared with the skirt; its bust shaping comes from the old dress volume. Sleeves are lofts that pass through the armhole (no modelled seam); the cuff is a plain gathered band.
Build is slimmer than the stout sprite.

Skirt: pleats are authored displacement, not simulated; weights are authored (pelvis / thigh / calf), so a long stride swings the hem wide and the trailing boot shows under the back hem. No cloth simulation or collision in engine is assumed.
Forearms are re-fitted MakeHuman base-mesh faces welded to the hands: plain anatomy, no elbow wrinkles, slightly paler than the face.
Kitchen stains are procedural (grease spots, pale dusting on the lap) and sparse.

No actions embedded; pose tests used the idle boundary pose and four samples of the Epic walk reference plus a hand-made turn. Not imported or seen in Unreal; Physics Asset not made. Validator: whole-mesh UV_OVERLAP error as for Dink (five texture sets); LOD0 over the soft triangle target.
